Name: EV1 Rear (beam axle on five links)
//PROVENANCE: Read this before treating any number in this file as an EV1 measurement.
LAYOUT - printed. EV1 chassis manual, printed page 271: 'The rear suspension on
the EV1 consists of a rear axle assembly with aluminum end castings and a
tubular center section. There are two coil springs, two twin tube shock
absorbers and five connecting links with non-replaceable bushings. These five
connecting links are composed of two upper suspension leading links, two lower
suspension trailing links, and a track bar.' This file builds exactly that
part list: one rigid Axle Tube carrying both spindles, two Lower Links and a
Track Bar as jointed bodies, two Upper Links as stiff spring-dampers, two
springs and two dampers, all chassis-mounted (see '//links' for why).
Chrono's SolidAxle template was not used: it is a steered axle (knuckles, tie
rod, drag link, bell crank) and has no track bar.
HARDPOINTS - from the ev1 repo's suspension baseline, programmerq/ev1 commit
a6ab7146d91dcdf4536ec2abfc72f979deb1c7d6 (PR #144),
geometry/suspension/ev1_suspension_hardpoints.csv. The table under
'//hardpoints_ev1_mm' copies each rear point with its tier and source, in the
body repair manual's datum frame (X rearward, Y to the car's right, Z up).
Only the rear spring's body seat and the lower link's body bracket are
printed coordinates (body repair manual p.158), and the lower bracket's ROLE
is inferred. The upper link body pivot is the midpoint of a printed two-bolt
bracket whose role is also inferred. Every other point is an estimate sized
to the printed envelope and the p.271 figure. None of them is measured.
FRAME MAP - inferred, not fitted. Chrono wants X forward, Y left, Z up, origin
at the vehicle file's 'Suspension Location'. The map anchors the baseline's
rear wheel centre (4198, 622, 408.2) on the spindle position the stand-in
file used, (0, 0.622, -0.08), so the car's ride height in the chassis frame
y = +Y/1000 for mirrored parts (Chrono gives the left side, the baseline the
right) and y = -Y/1000 for the one part that crosses the car, the track bar.
ALIGNMENT - printed. Camber -0.50 deg, toe 0.00 deg per wheel: chassis manual
p.61 rear nominals, fixed by the end castings. Track 1244 mm: chassis p.62.
SPRING, DAMPER, MASSES, BUSHINGS - see the '//' notes beside each. Nothing in
them is printed: the spring rate is the baseline's estimate, the free length
and damping are derived from it, and masses and link rates are estimates.
tests/test_suspension_geometry.cpp recomputes every Chrono coordinate below
from the '//hardpoints_ev1_mm' table through the frame map, so the table and
the coordinates cannot drift apart.

//frame.//: rr_wheel_centre in the baseline is inferred: X = front wheel centre + printed 2512 wheelbase, Y = half printed rear track, Z = derived ground + tyre loaded radius

lower_link_body.source: body repair manual p.158, redux datum-b158-17; baseline reads it as the lower trailing-link bracket (280 mm ahead of the axle)

lower_link_axle.source: baseline: under the axle tube on the end casting, same Y as the body pivot

upper_link_body.source: baseline: midpoint of printed bracket holes datum-b158-06/07 (body p.158), read as the upper leading-link bracket

upper_link_axle.source: baseline: on top of the end casting, above the lower link

spring_upper.source: body repair manual p.158, redux datum-b158-08; 640 mm spacing body p.161 dim-b161-06

spring_lower.source: baseline: spring pad on the axle straight below the body seat

damper_upper.source: baseline: twin-tube damper beside the spring; body mount not printed

damper_lower.source: baseline: on the end casting behind the axle tube

track_bar_body.source: baseline: single track bar 22145314; which side carries the body bracket is not printed, shown on the LEFT

track_bar_axle.source: baseline: axle end on the RIGHT casting, near level with the body end

Spindle.//: Mass, inertia and size carried over from the DoubleWishbone stand-in; not EV1 values.

Bodies.Name: Axle Tube
//: One rigid body for the aluminum end castings, tubular centre section, hubs and
electric drums. Mass 35.0 kg = 2 x 35 kg estimated rear unsprung corner
(baseline unsprung_mass_rear_corner) - 2 x (8.0 kg wheel + 7.5 kg tyre +
1.0 kg spindle, as this repo's wheel, tyre and spindle files carry them)
- half the 4.0 kg of jointed links (lower links, track bar) = 35.0 kg; the
upper links have no body (see '//links'), so their unsprung half stays in
this figure. Inertia: slender rod over the 1.244 m track, m L^2 / 12 about
X and Z; spin axis a 40 mm tube. Estimated.

Bodies.Name: Lower Link
Bodies.//: Trailing link, body end ahead of the axle. Position = midpoint of its two joints. Mass 1.0 kg estimated; inertia isotropic m L^2 / 12, L = 0.2596 m.

Bodies.Name: Track Bar
Bodies.//: Single part across the car (not mirrored). Position = midpoint of its two joints. Mass 2.0 kg estimated; inertia isotropic m L^2 / 12, L = 0.9405 m.

//links: The lower links and the track bar are bodies on kinematic spherical joints at
both ends. Those three constraints leave the axle free to bounce, roll, and
pitch about the lower links. The upper links take out that pitch, and they do
it as stiff spring-dampers ('Upper Link' under TSDAs) rather than jointed
bodies: four rigid fore-aft links of two different lengths over-constrain a
rigid axle, which only bushing compliance lets move (p.271: 'non-replaceable
bushings'), and Chrono's default Barzilai-Borwein solver refuses joint
bushings because they carry stiffness matrices. 2 kN/mm along the link with
2 kN s/m of damping is a generic rubber-bushed link rate, not EV1 data. Estimated.

TSDAs.Name: Upper Link
TSDAs.//: Leading link: body end behind the axle. Free Length = the 0.1566 m between its hardpoints, so it carries no load at the design position. Rates per '//links'.

TSDAs.Name: Spring
//: Rate 25311 N/m: the baseline's spring_rate_rear (estimated, a 1.5 Hz ride
target; the spring sits on the axle, motion ratio ~1). Free Length 0.2548 m is
derived: installed length 0.1448 m between the two seats above plus the static
load 2784 N / k, where 2784 N is half the rear-axle reaction of the chassis
mass and COM in ev1/chassis/EV1_Chassis.json. So the design position above is
the curb position and the stand-in's ride height carries over.

TSDAs.Name: Shock
//: 1710 N s/m: derived for a ride damping ratio of 0.30 (estimated; passenger cars
run about 0.2 to 0.4) on the spring above and the same 284 kg sprung corner,
divided by the square of the damper's 0.969 inclination ratio. The stand-in's
7000 N s/m was unsourced and would overdamp this spring (ratio ~1.3), leaving
the bounce test nothing to measure.

Axle.//: Driveline shaft inertia, carried over from the stand-in; the rear is undriven.
